name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about ten points on partisan fundamentals
Jacobs holds a large financial edge as incumbent with roughly $1.8 million raised and outside-group support
Challenger Ricardo Cabrera shows no reported fundraising or outside spending
No public general-election polling exists, limiting visibility
model.rationale: The district's ten-point Democratic lean, Jacobs's commanding fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing her near 96% all point to a comfortable incumbent win; the absence of any public polling keeps uncertainty wider than usual for a safe seat.
model.watch: Any polling showing a materially tighter race or significant outside spending on Cabrera's behalf would be the clearest sign to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 51st District leans Democratic by about ten points, and Representative Sara Jacobs is seeking reelection with the advantages of incumbency and a clear financial edge. She has raised roughly $1.8 million and draws outside-group support, while Republican Ricardo Cabrera shows no reported fundraising or outside spending. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have rated the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals.

Prediction markets give Jacobs roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat. The combination of a Democratic-leaning electorate, a well-funded incumbent, and a little-known challenger points to a comfortable Democratic victory, though the lack of polling means the exact margin carries more uncertainty than usual.
